question_bank.stem: A DQN implementation reaches a terminal state after taking an action. The target should be set to what value form?

options.text: Immediate reward plus gamma times the next maximum Q-value
Immediate reward without any discounted future Q-value
The average Q-value over the previous replay mini-batch
Zero for every terminal transition regardless of reward

question_bank.rationale: At a terminal state there is no future state to bootstrap from, so the target is just the immediate reward.

distractor_rationales.A: This is the non-terminal Bellman target and incorrectly adds nonexistent future value.
distractor_rationales.C: Replay sampling does not replace the terminal target rule.
distractor_rationales.D: Terminal rewards can be nonzero; they are not automatically discarded.

frame_evidence.description: Recap slide marks terminal-state handling in the DQN target with a red X over the future-Q branch.

question_bank.stem: A common DQN bug is applying the Bellman future term even after the episode ends. The lecture's implementation fix is to add what check?

options.text: A check that gamma equals exactly one
A check that the replay memory is empty
A check that the action was selected greedily
A Boolean check for whether the next state is terminal

question_bank.rationale: The instructor adds a terminal-state Boolean so the code can skip the future-Q term when s' ends the episode.

distractor_rationales.A: Gamma need not equal one and is unrelated to detecting terminal states.
distractor_rationales.B: Replay memory size does not determine whether the transition is terminal.
distractor_rationales.C: Greedy action choice is separate from terminal target handling.

source_ref.evidence_span: You would create a Boolean to detect terminal state.

frame_evidence.description: Recap slide marks terminal-state handling in the DQN target with a red X over the future-Q branch.

question_bank.stem: Experience replay changes training because a newly observed transition is stored and later sampled instead of being used in what one-pass way?

options.text: Training once on the newest transition and then moving on
Training only on terminal transitions from the final state
Training on generated labels from a supervised dataset
Training after removing all old states from memory

question_bank.rationale: Replay memory lets the agent revisit past experiences, improving reuse and decorrelating updates compared with one-pass online training.

distractor_rationales.B: Replay stores many transitions, not only terminal ones.
distractor_rationales.C: The transitions come from environment experience, not supervised labels.
distractor_rationales.D: Replay memory keeps old experiences rather than deleting them immediately.

source_ref.evidence_span: Experience replay is going to help

frame_evidence.description: Experience replay slide shows several experiences E1, E2, E3 stored in a replay memory bubble for later sampling.

question_bank.stem: The repeated mini-batch-of-cats analogy diagnoses what problem in sequential RL updates?

options.text: Targets are too small when gamma is below one
The Q-network has too few output neurons
Consecutive training samples can be highly correlated
Terminal rewards are unavailable after the episode

question_bank.rationale: Sequential trajectories can produce similar consecutive experiences, so replay introduces more diverse samples and less cross-correlation.

distractor_rationales.A: Discounting affects future reward valuation, not sample correlation.
distractor_rationales.B: Output dimensionality depends on action count, not sample ordering.
distractor_rationales.D: Terminal reward handling is a different DQN issue.

source_ref.evidence_span: It allows more reusability and less cross correlation

frame_evidence.description: Recap slide circles replay memory and notes sampling from memory when applying gradient descent.

question_bank.stem: When replay memory is added to DQN, gradient descent updates are computed from what training source?

options.text: Only the latest action's raw screen pixels
Only expert demonstrations from humans
Only the first state of each episode
Mini-batches sampled from stored past experiences

question_bank.rationale: The replay buffer supports mini-batch gradient descent over sampled experiences rather than only the latest transition.

distractor_rationales.A: Replay uses stored transitions, not just the latest pixels.
distractor_rationales.B: This is experience replay, not imitation learning.
distractor_rationales.C: Transitions from across episodes can be sampled, not just initial states.

source_ref.evidence_span: And you can use it with mini batch gradient descent.
